title: I Wanted to See the World

pages.title: My Father’s Truck
captions: I grew up in a coastal village in Xianxiang, Ningbo.
As a child, I often stayed in my dad's truck and travelled with him on deliveries.
That was my first glimpse of the world beyond home.
alt: A cargo truck on a road through a coastal village in Ningbo. A boy riding beside his father in the cab of a truck. The boy looking out of the truck window at the road beyond.

pages.title: New Year with My Sister
captions: Visits to relatives at Chinese New Year were my chance to see city life.
My sister would take me out to play. Those are some of my warmest childhood memories.
alt: An older sister and her little brother walk together through a city street, shown in a wide view, a view of their steps, and a quiet glance between them.

pages.title: A Road I Believed In
captions: I came to believe that studying hard was my way out.
A good university could open up more possibilities.
alt: The boy studying at a desk at home. The boy looking up from a book toward the window.

pages.title: Jumping and Running
captions: In fourth grade, I represented Xianxiang and won the Yinzhou district high jump competition.
I also came fourth in the 800 metres.
alt: A schoolboy clearing the bar in a high jump competition. The boy running an 800-metre race.

pages.title: The Court and the Track
captions: I started basketball in third grade. By sixth grade, I could do a between-the-legs layup.
I kept training. In junior high, I often won the school's 400- and 800-metre races.
alt: A boy performing a basketball layup. A junior-high student crossing the finish line.

pages.title: Catching Up
captions: My grades were uneven in my first two years of junior high.
In my final year, I caught up.
I qualified for a top provincial high school's special admissions exam.
alt: A junior-high student facing several school subjects. The student revising with growing concentration. The student looking hopeful about an admissions opportunity.

pages.title: Falling Short
captions: But I fell short of the minimum score.
That setback hit me hard. Its shadow stayed with me for years.
Under enormous pressure, I returned to preparing for the regular high school entrance exam.
alt: The student looking quietly disappointed by exam results. A student sitting alone after a disappointing exam. The student returning to his entrance-exam revision.

pages.title: Entering High School
captions: In the end, I finished first in my class.
I entered Zhengshi High School in Ningbo, still some way from what I had hoped for.
alt: A student walks into a busy school campus and later looks up in a stairwell, while other pupils play basketball.

pages.title: Other People’s Eyes
captions: As I grew through high school, my underbite became severe.
I was given hurtful nicknames and mocked.
I became painfully aware of how others saw me. My confidence faded.
Being around people gradually became stressful.
alt: A high-school student with a prominent lower jaw stands in a school corridor, holds his backpack strap and walks away from a group.

pages.title: A Light at Night
captions: Some nights, I hid in the dormitory bathroom and cried.
I woke early, stayed up late, and poured much of my time into studying.
In my last two years of high school, I often ranked first in my year. English had always come naturally to me.
alt: A quiet dormitory corridor and a student at the bathroom doorway. The student wiping away tears, with his pre-surgery jaw visible. The student studying under a warm desk lamp at night. The student concentrating on an English book.

pages.title: A Choice After the Exam
captions: My university entrance exam did not go as well as I had hoped.
I chose Zhejiang Gongshang University over a Project 211 university outside Zhejiang.
alt: A high-school graduate considering his university exam results. The graduate weighing his university choices.

pages.title: Teaching English
captions: I began teaching English after high school. I have kept teaching ever since.
alt: The young man beginning to teach English.

pages.title: French and University Life
captions: I loved languages and trusted my ability to learn them, so I chose to major in French.
As an undergraduate, I also studied cross-border e-commerce alongside French.
University gave me more freedom, but the distress over my jaw remained.
alt: An undergraduate opening a French coursebook. The undergraduate walking across campus before jaw surgery.

pages.title: My Family Beside Me
captions: My family took me to Shanghai Ninth People's Hospital for a consultation.
I decided to have corrective jaw surgery.
Before surgery, I needed orthodontic treatment.
alt: A young man and his family in a hospital waiting area. The family listening to a doctor during a consultation. An orthodontic appointment before jaw surgery.

pages.title: More Than Two Years
captions: It lasted more than two years, much longer than I had expected.
During treatment, my underbite became more pronounced, and the emotional strain grew.
I withdrew from social life and focused on studying. I consistently ranked first in my major, academically and overall.
alt: Calendar pages suggesting the long wait during treatment. An undergraduate sitting alone during orthodontic treatment. The undergraduate studying, his pre-surgery jaw clearly visible.

pages.title: The Long Wait Ends
captions: In the second semester of my junior year, I finally had surgery.
alt: The young man with a family member before surgery. The young man resting by a hospital window after surgery.

pages.title: Brighter Days
captions: Surgery changed my appearance. I began to regain the confidence to face everyday life.
Two months later, I secured recommended admission to the School of International Business at Southwestern University of Finance and Economics.
I also received the National Scholarship. After so much pressure and waiting, it was a bright moment in my life.
alt: A university student walking on campus after jaw surgery. The student receiving news of postgraduate admission. The student standing in warm campus light with a folder.

pages.title: An Internship in Hangzhou
captions: After securing my postgraduate place, I interned at Mingle Advisors, a Finnish firm in Hangzhou.
I worked on helping Finnish technology companies enter China, coordinating across languages and time zones.
alt: An internship in a small company office in Hangzhou.

pages.title: Working in French
captions: After graduation, I worked in French-speaking overseas sales at Market Union in Ningbo, helping close approximately US$1 million in orders.
From looking for suppliers to speaking with clients, language became part of the practical work.
alt: Working in overseas sales in Ningbo.

pages.title: Days in Chengdu
captions: Then I moved to Chengdu for graduate school.
Chengdu was a happy chapter. I studied, interned at Alliance Française, and continued teaching English.
At Alliance Française, I helped plan and carry out five Sino-French cultural events for more than 800 participants.
alt: Arriving in Chengdu for graduate study. Studying and preparing language lessons in Chengdu.

pages.title: Whether to Go to Paris
captions: Then came another choice: should I study abroad?
Going would mean delaying graduation.
I thought about it for a long time. Since childhood, I had wanted to see the world.
I chose a one-year exchange at Paris 1 Panthéon-Sorbonne University.
alt: Reading about an overseas exchange programme. Weighing the exchange against a later graduation. A window scene echoing the childhood truck journeys. Preparing exchange application papers and a travel bag.

pages.title: Finding My Way to AI
captions: Before leaving, I spent four months in overseas talent recruitment at ByteDance in Chengdu.
I helped ByteDance's Seed AI team recruit top talent in North America.
I helped build an AI talent database covering more than 400 professors, 900 PhD researchers and 200 master’s students.
I also supported TikTok LIVE’s local talent searches in Germany, France and the UK.
That experience drew me into AI and pushed me to learn more.
alt: An overseas recruitment internship in Chengdu. Supporting a remote talent recruitment conversation. Learning about AI through books and notes.

pages.title: Studying in Paris
captions: With a new direction taking shape, I left for Paris.
At Panthéon-Sorbonne University, I studied international law.
alt: A young man walks through an airport, looks through an airplane window and attends a university class in Paris.

pages.title: Another Language
captions: During my year in Paris, I also spent a year learning Spanish.
alt: An exchange student taking notes in a Spanish-language class in Paris.

pages.title: The Boundaries of My World
captions: I have always loved languages. I explored Paris, France, and other parts of Europe.
The limits of my language are the limits of my world.
The child who wanted to see the world had finally made it.
alt: A young man walks through Paris beside the Seine and pauses at a stone railing with a notebook.

pages.title: Cloud, AI and Learning
captions: After returning from Paris, I joined Tencent Cloud as a direct sales intern.
My experience with AI helped me find my direction. I keep building with AI and learning more about cloud computing.
Today I am a trainee rotating through technology, product and business at Tencent Cloud.
My current work in technical sales brings me into contact with media AIGC clients and AI-native startups.
alt: Colleagues discuss their work; the young man looks at and shares an account-workspace interface with a small penguin mascot.

pages.title: Still Teaching English
captions: I have taught English since leaving high school. Years of experience have only deepened my enthusiasm for teaching.
alt: The teacher sits beside a learner, writes in an open book and talks with her across the table.

pages.title: Still Curious
captions: Languages opened up my world. And there is still so much I want to explore.
alt: A hand closes a red book; the young man packs it into a bag and looks over a city from an open space.
